paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.English: The chart titled “Error (RTE)” illustrates measured error values on the RTE task for two methods, LoRA and QLoRA, across different adapter ranks. The horizontal axis contains the categorical rank values labeled “Rank,” shown in increasing order as 4, 16, 64, and 256, while the vertical axis is an unlabeled numeric scale (linear) with visible tick marks at approximately 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9, spanning roughly from 0.3 at the bottom to about 1.2 at the top of the plotting area. Bars are grouped by rank with two side-by-side bars per group: a blue bar for “LoRA” and a green bar for “QLoRA,” as indicated by the legend placed near the top of the plot. At rank 4, the LoRA (blue) bar is around 0.59 and the QLoRA (green) bar is around 0.54; at rank 16, LoRA is around 0.61 and QLoRA around 0.45; at rank 64, LoRA is around 0.70 and QLoRA around 0.50; and at rank 256, LoRA is around 0.75 and QLoRA around 0.63. Each bar includes a black error bar with caps, showing variability around the bar heights, with visually larger uncertainty for LoRA at rank 64 and moderate-sized error bars in the other groups. No bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent color coding and the presence of error bars, and the grouping is strictly by the ascending rank categories.
model_annotations.German: The chart titled “Error (RTE)” illustrates error values for the RTE task across different adapter ranks, with two methods shown as side-by-side bars (LoRA and QLoRA) and uncertainty indicated by vertical error bars. The horizontal axis contains the categorical rank values labeled “Rank,” shown in ascending order as 4, 16, 64, and 256. The vertical axis represents the error magnitude (implied by the title), displayed on a linear scale with visible tick labels at approximately 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 (regular spacing of about 0.3), and the plotted values extend from roughly 0.3 up to around 1.0. For each rank, there are two grouped bars: a blue bar for LoRA and a green bar for QLoRA (as indicated by the legend in the upper-left). At rank 4, the LoRA bar is approximately 0.58 with a small black error bar, and the QLoRA bar is approximately 0.52 with a similar error bar; at rank 16, LoRA is about 0.60 while QLoRA is about 0.45; at rank 64, LoRA is about 0.69–0.70 while QLoRA is about 0.48; and at rank 256, LoRA is about 0.74–0.75 while QLoRA is about 0.62–0.63. The error bars are drawn in black with caps for each bar, and no individual bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent use of color and the legend.
